name: a first-look marker keeps an event on a day hidden behind "N more" from accusing an agent
notes: §3 v1.10: every row a Calendar pass stores as a first sighting gets a first-look marker: a gcal.event entry of the same observer and account, window = the row's occurredAt (a point), lastSyncAt = changesSince = the row's first sighting. A marker blocks its row by orphan rule (b) and never makes coverage full.

Coverage. acct-a follows the week [10-04 00:00, 10-11 00:00]: changesSince 09:00, last synced 14:20. acct-b first looks at the same week at 14:10, but 10-08 hides events behind "N more": the pass reports one entry per run of whole days, [10-04 00:00, 10-08 00:00] and [10-09 00:00, 10-11 00:00], and, not having seen the week whole, records them without changesSince (§3). acct-b's marker for o1: window [10-08 10:00, 10-08 10:00], changesSince = lastSyncAt = 14:10. No claims.
o1 'Busy day' (10-08 10:00): a chip acct-b's pass read on the hidden day, stored as a first sighting at 14:10. No window of acct-b holds 10-08 10:00.

o1 (§3): the entries holding 10-08 10:00 are acct-a's (changesSince 09:00 < 14:10 ≤ 14:20: rule (a) holds) and the marker (changesSince 14:10 = o1's first sighting: rule (b) fails). Not an orphan → no receipt.

Without the marker, o1 would be an orphan (acct-b's runs leave its day out) and, anchored at 14:10, muse's session at 14:08 (4000) and idle [14:05, 14:12] covering [14:08, 14:10] (3000) give 7/10 → a false UNASKED for an event already on the calendar (Hard Rule 7).

o2 'Team lunch' (10-07 12:30), first seen 14:20 by acct-a's pass: acct-a's entry followed changes since 09:00 < 14:20 ≤ 14:20. acct-b's run [10-04, 10-08] holds 10-07 12:30 but compared nothing and was synced at 14:10 < 14:20, so it did not find o2 already there → an orphan. Anchor 14:20: muse's session at 14:18 (4000), idle [14:15, 14:25] covers [14:18, 14:20] (3000) → 7/10 → UNASKED, reasons unasked.session, unasked.idle.
o2 finality (§7): muse's adapter synced 15:00 ≥ 14:20 + 2 + 30 min = 14:52 → FINAL (evaluatedAt 15:30).
